messages:
Alex: early morning debrief — two small but noisy pages overnight, want to handoff state before I sign off. TL;DR: embed-autoscaler oscillation + one KV leader with a stale kernel causing eviction churn. Customer impact low but visible in streaming p95. Details below.

IncidentBot: Pager triggered: embed-autoscaler | us-west-2 (pager #4532) at 2026-03-09T02:12:08Z — auto-resolved 02:40:12Z

Alex: timeline: 02:10 saw p95 spike to ~1.6s for streaming tokens, 02:12 autoscaler doubled pods and then dropped, 02:20 we observed a single kv leader node with continuous jemalloc growth + evictions. By 02:30 we pinned traffic off that node and latency returned to baseline.

Tess: thanks. I'm primary for the next 12h — I'll take ongoing monitoring and customer comms if anything flares. Sam, you OK as secondary? :point_right:

Sam: yep, I'm secondary. I'll keep an eye on the embed autoscaler alarming windows and look at rollout history for any recent changes. Added a quick dashboard watchlist.

Maria: created INF-1234 to track follow-up (runtime/kv): "kv leader kernel mismatch causing eviction churn" — assigned to runtime team. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INF-1234

Lee: brief mitigation notes I ran during the incident:
```
# commands used to shift traffic away from bad leader
kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep kv-leader-node
kubectl -n runtime label node/kv-node-17 maintenance=true
# scale down aggressive autoscaler step temporarily
kubectl -n autoscaler patch config autoscaler-config --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxScaleStep":1}}'
```

Alex: customer impact summary to put on the incident page: ~0.8% of streaming requests in us-west-2 experienced higher p95 and rare truncated streams between 02:10–02:30. No 5xx spike, no ingestion loss. Most requests retried successfully.

Tess: next steps I own: 1) keep the maintenance label on kv-node-17 until runtime can repro (ETA 24h), 2) confirm autoscaler config rollback tomorrow AM, 3) prepare a short note for support to send to customers if asked.

Sam: I'll add a temporary alert tweak: extend the autoscaler cooldown detection from 30s -> 90s so we don't get tight oscillation noise during warmup. Will notify infra change channel after patch.

Maria: runtime asked for the kernel/build info from kv-node-17 — grabbed `/var/log/dmesg` and pod logs, attached to INF-1234. Runtime suspects a backported patch mismatch.

Alex: ops-runbook pointers (for whoever takes the follow-up): https://docs.redwood.example/runbooks/kv-leader-eviction AND https://docs.redwood.example/playbooks/autoscaler-oscillation — both have recovery steps and diag commands.

Lee: coverage note — APAC overnight window tomorrow might be lightly staffed. Tess, you're primary but can we get someone in the roster for 03:00–07:00 UTC to cover potential reoccurrence? Need another person for overlap.

Tess: I can push a calendar ping to the oncall rota and ask DevEx for one extra shift volunteer. If no volunteer we escalate to Sam for overlap.

IncidentBot: Incident summary posted to #incidents at 2026-03-09T03:05:00Z — incident ID INC-2026-0319-07

Sam: action items tracked:
- [ ] INF-1234 (runtime) — root cause and kernel alignment. (Maria)
- [ ] Autoscaler cooldown tweak and test. (Sam)
- [ ] Keep maintenance label + hardware diag on kv-node-17. (Tess/Alex)
- [ ] Customer comms draft if asked. (Tess)

Alex: leaving handoff. If anything pops, page as usual. I'm logging off now. Thanks team :raised_hands:

Tess: got it. I'm on watch. Will update this thread if anything changes.

Sam: standing by for overlap. Good handoff.

Maria: added logs and core dumps to INF-1234. Will ping runtime lead.

Lee: added a short checklist to the runbook with the exact `kubectl` commands and the autoscaler config keys we changed. Saved as runbook edit v1.2.

Tess: last message before I start monitoring: if you see repeated evictions please run `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and check `OOMKilled` vs `Evicted` reason, and add a screenshot to INF-1234.

IncidentBot: thread closed for now — no active pages in the past 30m.
